rules.statement: Do not put commit SHAs, pipeline run IDs, or timestamps in cloud resource tags; tag resources only with static ownership values such as `source` (repository and root) and `managed_by`.
rules.why: Tags that change on every apply rewrite every resource, keep plans from ever showing "no changes", and hide real drift from scheduled drift detection. A SHA on a resource the apply didn't touch also says nothing about the code that defines it.
rules.check: Look for tag maps in OpenTofu/Terraform code that use values like commit, sha, run_id, run_attempt, github.sha, timestamp(), or other values that change per run.

rules.statement: Build every container image, Helm chart, and published module artifact in GitHub Actions with a build-provenance attestation and a keyless Sigstore signature, and reference deployed artifacts by digest, not by mutable tag.
rules.why: Provenance that travels with the artifact can be checked at deployment time and never causes drift. Trusting by convention that `main` is what runs gives no verification.
rules.check: Look for build/publish workflows that are missing attest-build-provenance or cosign keyless signing steps, and for deployment manifests or Flux sources that point at images or charts by tag with no @sha256 digest.

rules.statement: Configure Flux to verify an artifact's Sigstore signature against the identity of the workflow that built it before applying a release, and admit only signed images from the platform registry into the cluster.
rules.why: Without verification at the point of deployment, nothing proves that the running workload came from the reviewed code.
rules.check: Look for Flux OCIRepository/HelmRepository sources that have no `verify` block with cosign keyless identity matching, and for admission policies that allow unsigned images or images from other registries.

rules.statement: Make CI assume AWS roles with the session name `gh-<run_id>-<run_attempt>`, and have the role trust policy enforce that form with an `sts:RoleSessionName` condition.
rules.why: CloudTrail then attributes every API call to the exact workflow run, and through it to the commit and approver. CI can't get credentials without naming its run.
rules.check: Look for configure-aws-credentials steps that are missing `role-session-name: gh-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}`, and for GitHub OIDC role trust policies that have no `sts:RoleSessionName` condition.

rules.statement: Give each CI scope its own named Cloudflare API token instead of sharing one token across pipelines.
rules.why: Cloudflare's audit log can then attribute each change to a specific pipeline scope.
rules.check: Look for workflows or jobs for different scopes that reuse the same Cloudflare token secret.

rules.statement: Run every infrastructure apply job in a GitHub environment.
rules.why: GitHub then records a deployment with the commit, run, and approval, which answers "which commit is live in production".
rules.check: Look for workflow jobs that run `tofu apply`/`terraform apply` without an `environment:` key.

rules.statement: Do not add OpenTofu-managed "last deployed" records (for example an SSM parameter holding the current commit) to track which commit is deployed.
rules.why: Such a record shows a diff on every apply, which blinds drift detection. GitHub deployments already answer the question.
rules.check: Look for managed resources whose value is set from the commit SHA or run metadata.
